art.snowLine: 0.62 of the levels (the top 38% take alt-7, and alt-8 from 0.85)
art.engine: heightField (seeded peaks + simplex noise) -> contourLevels (marching squares, smoothed rings) -> relief (each level lifted one step, filled flat), with bleed past the frame and a minArea speck filter
uses: hero range (9 levels under the sky)

name.purpose: The owner's name in the hero and footer, sized from its length to run margin to margin; never wraps from 48rem. Nepali ceiling 12vw (19vw on phones).

title.purpose: Page titles and the next project.

head.purpose: Section headings. Nepali starts at 1.875rem on phones: clamp(1.875rem, 0.845rem + 4.24vw, 4.5rem).

statement.purpose: Quotations and large running statements, in Eczar 500.

lead.purpose: One intro sentence under a heading, figure lines, contact lines.

small.purpose: Metadata and captions, muted, sentence case.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The one ease for every transition and animation.

motion.name: dur-1
motion.purpose: Hover colour and underline changes, button press.

motion.name: dur-3
motion.purpose: The name rising in, picture zoom on hover.

motion.name: hm-lift
motion.purpose: The range lifts from the flat map into relief on load, in three altitude bands, transform only.

motion.name: hm-spread
motion.purpose: Scrolling past the hero spreads the sheets apart.

motion.name: drift
motion.purpose: Cursor drift on fine pointers, after hydration.

motion.name: hm-rise-in
motion.purpose: Section parts rise into view, staggered by --hm-i.

motion.name: hm-zoom-settle
motion.purpose: Archival pictures settle while scrolling past.

motion.name: view-transition
motion.purpose: A project's mountain morphs into its case study.

motion.name: hm-progress
motion.purpose: The article's ink reading line, 4px, across the top.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: All of the above off; content is visible and at rest by default.

components.name: Printed Relief
components.description: The signature: flat altitude sheets, each lifted one step, snow above the snow line, under flat sky bands.

narrative.overview:
The site has one picture: the Himalaya seen from Kathmandu, printed like a multi-block woodblock print. Each altitude is one flat sheet of colour, lifted one step above the one below, under a sky of flat bands lit for the real hour in Kathmandu. Everything else stays quiet so that picture and the type can carry the page.

Pages are long and spacious. Sections sit far apart and each one owns a whole field of colour: snow, a second snow, ridge blue, pine, night or rhododendron. Nothing is a card and nothing floats above the page at rest. Type does the structural work: Eczar display headings in both scripts, a fitted name that runs margin to margin, and plain text in Inter and Noto Sans Devanagari.

The system lives under `.himal` with `hm-` utilities (`src/styles/himal.css`), so the admin's Graphite system is untouched. Implementation detail, budgets and pitfalls live in docs/guides/portfolio.md ("Design system: Himal") and decisions 0179 to 0184.
keyCharacteristics: Flat altitude sheets as the one picture, generated from a seed, the same markup on server and browser.
Whole-section colour fields; no cards, gradients, shadows at rest or hairline rules.
One red, for what can be acted on.
Eczar display in Latin and Devanagari; five type sizes.
Motion that moves only transform, clip-path and colour, and switches off under reduced motion.

rules.name: The One Red Rule
rules.body: Rhododendron marks only what can be acted on, plus the contact field. Active states, selection, quote marks, list markers and the reading line use ink or muted. There are no status colours.

rules.name: The Whole Field Rule
rules.body: A section takes one whole ground and the inks that read on it (`hm-field-*`). Neighbouring sections never share a field. Fields are never cards, insets or tinted boxes.

rules.name: The Contrast Floor Rule
rules.body: Every text pair is at least 4.5:1 on its ground and its second ground, in both themes, on every field and on the art (`tests/unit/himal-tokens.test.ts`). Text on a new colour adds a pair there.

rules.name: The Five Sizes Rule
rules.body: Small, body, lead, head and title do all the work; the fitted name is the only exception. No other sizes enter a page.

rules.name: The Figures Are Facts Rule
rules.body: A number is set at its sentence's size, in Eczar semibold beside the sentence it belongs to. It is never a headline or a big stat.

rules.name: The Devanagari Rule
rules.body: Nepali display type drops the negative tracking and opens the leading. Nepali headings start at 30px on phones and reach the English size on wide screens. The name gets a lower ceiling.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: No uppercase labels, no letter-spaced small caps, no eyebrows above headings.

rules.name: The Flat Print Rule
rules.body: Every surface is a flat fill. Depth belongs to the art, made of stacked sheets, never to the interface.

dos: Do give each section one whole field (`hm-field-*`) and never repeat a neighbour's field.
Do reserve rhododendron for actions, link hover, focus and errors, plus the contact field.
Do use ink or muted for active states, selection, quote marks, list markers and the reading line.
Do set display type in Eczar in both scripts, and text in Inter and Noto Sans Devanagari.
Do keep to the five sizes, and set figures at their sentence's size.
Do keep buttons square, filled and 48px tall.
Do draw new art with the terrain engine: flat altitude sheets, lifted one step, with the snow line and the bleed.
Do animate only transform, translate, clip-path and colour, and switch it all off under reduced motion.
Do credit every archival picture and record its provenance beside the file.
donts: Don't use gradients, including in the sky.
Don't add shadows at rest, blur or floating surfaces.
Don't draw hairline rules or borders to divide content; change the field instead.
Don't add eyebrows, index numbers or uppercase labels.
Don't round corners on interface elements.
Don't use JetBrains Mono outside code blocks.
Don't set a figure as a headline-sized stat.
